names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 22 Απριλίου, «Άγιος Πλάτων ο Ιερομάρτυρας επίσκοπος Μπάνια Λούκα», with the rank words and the see left off; the page gives his name in the world as Milivoje Jovanović, in Greek letters.

Read out of the title on the name link behind the line for 22 апреля ст. ст., name page 14507, «Святитель Платон (Йованович), епископ Бянолукский», with the rank word before the name and the see after it left off; the day’s own line gives the genitive «Платона» without the surname. The surname is part of the name and stays, per BRIEF-RUSSIAN §2. Measured against the gate’s own key function before it was written: 'иованович платон' has no other holder in the corpus.

birth.note: saint.gr: «γεννήθηκε στις 29 Σεπτεμβρίου 1874 μ.Χ. στο Βελιγράδι», and the page heads him «(1874 - 1941)».

death.note: saint.gr: «Οι Ουστάτσι τον συνέλαβαν μαζί με τον ιερέα Δουσάν (Σούμποτιτς) και τον εκτέλεσαν», in the year 1941 of the German occupation which the page has just dated, and it heads him «(1874 - 1941)».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 22 апреля ст. ст. — «Сщмч. Платона , еп. Банялукского (1941).»
source.note: The day’s sixth entry, and THE RUSSIAN CALENDAR GIVES HIM NO LIFE PAGE: the line carries a name link and no life link, and the name page behind it, 14507, prints the title and «День памяти: 22 апреля» and nothing else. What it gives that the line does not is the surname, «Платон (Йованович)», which is the form stored here. THE TWO SPELL THE SEE DIFFERENTLY: the line reads «еп. Банялукского» and the name page’s own title «епископ Бянолукский», which looks like a slip for the first; the folder’s `office`, Bishop of Banja Luka, was not touched. The year 1941 is the year the folder already held off saint.gr, and `dates` was not changed. No second day anywhere on the page. Not checked: azbyka.ru.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 22ας Απριλίου — «Άγιος Πλάτων ο Ιερομάρτυρας επίσκοπος Μπάνια Λούκα»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 22 Απριλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The page is a full and dated life: born 29 September 1874 at Belgrade to Ilija Jovanović and Jelka Sokolović; a monk, then deacon and priest; sent in 1896 to the theological academy of Moscow and back in 1901 as superior of the monastery of Rakovica and a teacher; a military chaplain in the First World War and afterwards a carer for orphans and the wounded; elected bishop of Ohrid in 1938 and moved in 1939 to Banja Luka in northern Bosnia; refusing in 1941 to leave his flock when the pro-Nazi Croatian government demanded that the Orthodox Serbs convert or go; seized by the Ustaše with the priest Dušan Subotić and executed, his body thrown into the river Vrbanja and recovered a few days later by Christians of the village of Kumsale, who buried it in the military cemetery of Banja Luka; his relics translated in 1973 to the cathedral of Banja Luka; and his canonisation by the Holy Synod of the Church of Serbia in 1998. **The Serbian row here is still `undocumented`**, although the page names the Serbian synod as the body that canonised him: the row records what was read, and pravoslavno.rs was not read. The corpus keeps several saints named Plato or Platon — of Ancyra, of Megara, the venerable, Aivazidis and Kulbusch — and none of them is this bishop. It prints no hymn.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue on pravoslavno.rs for the corresponding Julian day (30 September 2026).
